procedural_history.originating_court: IInd Additional Sessions Judge, Baloda Bazar, Dist.Raipur
procedural_history.impugned_order: Judgment and order of the High Court dated 06.04.2015 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court of Chhattisgarh dismissing the Criminal Appeal No.3 of 2010 titled Statrughan vs. State of Chhattisgarh
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court of Chhattisgarh dismissed Criminal Appeal No. 3 of 2010, thereby affirming the conviction under section 302, Indian Penal Code and the sentence to undergo life imprisonment along with fine of Rs.5,000/- passed by the IInd Additional Sessions Judge.
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The accused appellant assailed the correctness of the High Court's judgment and order in the Supreme Court. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal.

directions: The appellant is acquitted of all the charges.
The appellant shall be released forthwith, if not wanted in any other case.

issue.issue_text: Whether the prosecution had established the charge against the appellant.

facts: The Supreme Court found that there were no eyewitnesses who had actually seen the appellant assaulting the deceased.
The Court determined that the prosecution's story was not probable.
The evidence provided by the prosecution's witnesses of fact was found to not inspire confidence and contained material contradictions.
law: In a criminal case, the burden of proof is on the prosecution to establish the charge against the accused beyond a reasonable doubt.
application: The Supreme Court analyzed the evidence on record and first determined that there was no direct evidence, as no eyewitness saw the actual assault.
The Court then evaluated the supporting evidence from the witnesses of fact.
It concluded that this evidence was unreliable due to material contradictions and did not inspire confidence.
Based on these weaknesses, the Court found the entire prosecution story to be improbable.
Given the lack of credible direct or supporting evidence, the Court held that the prosecution had not met its burden of proving the charge.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the prosecution had failed to establish the charge against the appellant. Consequently, the Court allowed the appeal, set aside the conviction and sentence from the lower courts, and acquitted the appellant.

issue.issue_text: Whether any of the eye-witnesses had actually seen the occurrence of the appellant assaulting the deceased.

facts: The Court explicitly stated that the answer to whether any eyewitnesses saw the appellant assaulting the deceased is 'no'.
Witnesses PW-2 (wife of PW-1), PW-3 (the deceased's widow), and PW-4 (daughter of PW-1) all arrived at the scene but none of them testified to seeing the appellant commit the assault.
The only evidence from a witness at the scene (PW-1) was that he saw the appellant running away from the location when he arrived.
PW-1 himself stated that the deceased was already unconscious and not in a condition to speak when he reached him.
Another witness, PW-14, testified that PW-1 initially only told him that the deceased had been assaulted, without naming the appellant as the attacker.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court decided that none of the eye-witnesses had actually seen the appellant assaulting the deceased by systematically analyzing the testimony of each witness who was present at the scene. The Court found that while witnesses arrived after hearing a cry, none of them actually saw the assault take place. The key witness, PW-1, only saw the appellant running away and found the victim already unconscious, contradicting the idea that he was a direct eyewitness to the attack.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the prosecution had established the charge against the appellant.
appellant_arguments: The lower courts erred by relying on inadmissible evidence and ignoring relevant admissible evidence.
The witnesses of fact were inconsistent and did not inspire confidence.
The medical evidence did not support the prosecution's story.
The case was based on circumstantial and hearsay evidence, with no direct evidence of the crime.
The prosecution failed to establish any motive.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution had fully proved the commission of the crime with cogent material.
The defense failed to disturb or shake the evidence of the prosecution witnesses during cross-examination.
There is no reason to interfere with the concurrent findings of the lower courts.

arguments.issue_text: Whether any of the eye-witnesses had actually seen the occurrence of the appellant assaulting the deceased.
appellant_arguments: There was no direct evidence of the commission of the crime.
The case was based on circumstantial and hearsay evidence.
None of the witnesses who reached the place of occurrence (PW-2, PW-3, PW-4) stated that they had seen the appellant assaulting the deceased.
The only evidence was from PW-1, who merely saw the appellant running away from the scene after the deceased was already unconscious and unable to speak.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution's evidence was cogent and sufficient to prove the crime.
The defense was unable to discredit the prosecution witnesses.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: The provided text does not contain a binding legal rule (ratio decidendi). It only states the final outcome of the case, which is that the prosecution failed to establish the charge, leading to the appellant's acquittal.
obiter: The text does not contain any non-binding observations (obiter dicta).

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The prosecution failed to establish the charge against the appellant because its story was not probable, the supporting evidence from the witnesses of fact did not inspire confidence and contained material contradictions, and no motive for the crime was established, which is critical in a case with no direct eyewitnesses.
legal_tests_applied: In a case where there is no eye-witness to the incident, the prosecution has to establish a motive for the commission of the crime.
While motive may not have a major role in a case with direct evidence, it has an important role to play when, as in the present case, no one has seen the occurrence.
